blocks.text: Turkey and Jordan may be close geographically, but they give you two very different trips. In Turkey, you can begin with the streets and monuments of Istanbul or the valleys of Cappadocia. A short flight later, Jordan changes the setting completely, with Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Dead Sea forming the core of the journey.

Our Turkey & Jordan Tours range from 9 to 13 days. Shorter itineraries deliberately focus on either Istanbul or Cappadocia before continuing to Jordan, while longer routes can add Ephesus, Pamukkale, Jerash, Madaba, Mount Nebo, and more time around Petra and Wadi Rum.

Depending on the itinerary, arrangements can include hotels, guided sightseeing with local guides, airport transfers, regional and domestic flights, and private transportation. Private Tours, Small Group Tours, and Customized Tours are available on selected programs.

sections.heading: Turkey & Jordan Tours at a Glance

rows: Istanbul or Cappadocia • Petra • Wadi Rum

blocks.text: This is the first decision to make if you are looking at one of the shorter tours.

Choose Istanbul if you want the Turkey portion to concentrate on history, architecture, local neighborhoods, and the Bosphorus before flying to Jordan. It creates a city-and-history route that changes considerably once you reach Petra and Wadi Rum.

Cappadocia makes for a different trip. Instead of beginning in a large city, you start among valleys, cave settlements, and volcanic landscapes before moving on to the sandstone terrain of southern Jordan.
Both work. The better choice depends on which part of Turkey you would be more disappointed to miss.

sections.heading: How Much of Jordan Should You Include?

blocks.text: Petra is naturally at the center of most Turkey and Jordan itineraries, but it should not automatically be treated as the only reason to visit the country.

Wadi Rum is the natural next step on many routes, particularly if you want to spend a night in the desert. With more time, the journey can include the Dead Sea as well as Jerash, Madaba, and Mount Nebo.

Because Jordan is mainly travelled overland, these places can be connected without adding domestic flights. What matters is allowing enough time so that Petra and Wadi Rum do not become quick stops between long driving days.

sections.heading: What Changes When You Add More Days?

blocks.text: A 9-day Turkey & Jordan Tour needs to make choices. Focusing on Istanbul or Cappadocia rather than trying to cover both gives Jordan enough room for Petra and Wadi Rum.
With around 11 days, more of Turkey can be included before the flight to Jordan, or the additional time can be used to expand the Jordan section.

At 13 days, it becomes practical to build a broader route through both countries, adding places such as Ephesus or Pamukkale in Turkey and the Dead Sea or northern Jordan without making every day another transfer.
The extra days are most useful when they improve the pace, not when they are simply used to add more names to the itinerary.

sections.heading: Flying to Jordan and Travelling Overland

blocks.text: The international connection between the two countries is normally by air, with Amman serving as the main gateway in Jordan.

Turkey may require domestic flights when the itinerary combines Istanbul with Cappadocia or western Turkey. Once in Jordan, the journey works differently. Amman, Jerash, Madaba, the Dead Sea, Petra, and Wadi Rum are generally connected by road.
This difference in transportation is one reason the combination works well: the Turkey section can cover greater distances by air, while Jordan becomes a more continuous overland journey.

Spring and autumn are generally the easiest seasons for combining Turkey and Jordan. March through May and September through November work particularly well when the itinerary includes outdoor sightseeing in Cappadocia, Petra, and Wadi Rum.

Summer is possible, but Jordan can be very hot, particularly around the Dead Sea and southern regions. Winter is quieter and cooler. Cappadocia may have snow, while Petra and Wadi Rum can become cold after sunset.
Rather than choosing the season for one country alone, consider where you expect to spend the most time outdoors.
For a shorter trip, decide first whether Istanbul or Cappadocia matters more to you. That single choice will shape much of the Turkey portion without forcing too many stops into nine days.

With additional time, you can broaden the Turkey route or see more of Jordan beyond Petra and Wadi Rum. If an existing itinerary is close but the balance does not quite suit you, selected Customized Tours can adjust the number of nights, hotels, and overall pace.
If you would rather concentrate entirely on Jordan, browse our Jordan Tours. For different regional combinations, see our Turkey & Egypt Tours or Turkey, Greece & Egypt Tours.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for a Turkey and Jordan tour?
faqs.a: Most travelers recommend spending 9 to 13 days exploring Turkey and Jordan. This allows enough time to visit Istanbul, Cappadocia, Amman, Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Dead Sea without rushing. Longer itineraries can also include Ephesus or Pamukkale for a more complete Turkey experience.

faqs.q: What is the best Turkey and Jordan itinerary for first-time visitors?
faqs.a: A classic first-time itinerary includes Istanbul, Cappadocia, Amman, Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Dead Sea. This route combines Turkey's historic cities, unique landscapes, and rich cultural heritage with Jordan's ancient archaeological sites, spectacular desert scenery, and famous natural attractions in one well-balanced journey.

faqs.q: What is included in a Turkey and Jordan tour package?
faqs.a: Most tour packages include carefully selected hotels, airport transfers, licensed local guides, sightseeing, transportation listed in the itinerary, daily breakfast, and domestic or regional flights where applicable. Individual inclusions vary by itinerary, allowing travelers to choose the package that best matches their travel style and budget.

faqs.q: Are Turkey and Jordan tours available as private or small group tours?
faqs.a: You can choose between Private Tours, Small Group Tours, or fully Customized Tours. Private tours provide maximum flexibility and personalized sightseeing, while small group tours offer excellent value with shared experiences. Customized itineraries allow you to adjust hotels, travel dates, destinations, activities, and overall tour duration.

faqs.q: Can I customize my Turkey and Jordan itinerary?
faqs.a: Yes. Every itinerary can be personalized according to your travel interests, available vacation time, accommodation preferences, sightseeing priorities, and budget. You may extend your stay, add destinations such as Ephesus or the Dead Sea, upgrade hotels, or include additional cultural and outdoor experiences.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Turkey and Jordan?
faqs.a: The best time to visit Turkey and Jordan is during spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November). Mild temperatures make sightseeing comfortable in Istanbul, Cappadocia, Petra, Wadi Rum, and the Dead Sea, while pleasant weather creates ideal conditions for outdoor activities throughout both countries.

Jordan is widely regarded as one of the safest countries in the Middle East for international visitors. Popular destinations such as Petra, Wadi Rum, Amman, Jerash, and the Dead Sea welcome millions of travelers each year, supported by a well-developed tourism infrastructure and experienced local hospitality professionals.

faqs.q: Is Petra included in every Turkey and Jordan tour?
faqs.a: Most Turkey and Jordan itineraries include Petra because it is Jordan's most famous attraction and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Depending on the itinerary length, your tour may also include Wadi Rum, the Dead Sea, Jerash, Madaba, and Amman for a more complete Jordan experience.

faqs.q: Can I visit Petra in one day?
faqs.a: Yes. A full-day visit allows enough time to experience Petra's most famous landmarks, including the Treasury, Street of Facades, Royal Tombs, and the Roman Theater. Travelers wishing to hike to the Monastery or explore lesser-known trails may prefer spending additional time there.

faqs.q: Is the Jordan Pass worth buying?
faqs.a: The Jordan Pass offers excellent value for many international visitors by combining visa fee exemptions for eligible travelers with entry to Petra and numerous historical attractions across Jordan. Whether it is worthwhile depends on your nationality, itinerary, and the sites included in your tour package.

faqs.q: Do I need separate visas for Turkey and Jordan?
faqs.a: Visa requirements depend on your nationality. Some travelers qualify for visa-free entry or electronic visas, while others require separate visas for Turkey and Jordan. Before booking, we recommend checking the latest official entry requirements based on your passport and intended travel dates.

faqs.q: Is transportation included between Turkey and Jordan?
faqs.a: Yes. Most combined itineraries include the required regional flight between Turkey and Jordan, together with airport transfers and all transportation listed in the itinerary. Our destination specialists coordinate flights, hotels, and local services to ensure a smooth and well-organized travel experience.

faqs.q: Can I combine Turkey and Jordan with another country?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Many travelers extend their vacation by adding Egypt, Greece, Israel, or Morocco. Our Multi Country Tours combine flights, hotels, licensed local guides, airport transfers, and sightseeing into one professionally coordinated itinerary, making it easy to explore several countries during a single journey.

faqs.q: Are licensed local guides included throughout the tour?
faqs.a: Yes. Guided sightseeing is conducted by experienced, licensed local guides in both Turkey and Jordan. Their local expertise provides valuable historical and cultural insights while helping you better understand each destination through informative tours, authentic experiences, and personalized recommendations.

faqs.q: Why book your Turkey and Jordan tour with Magnificent Travel?
faqs.a: Since 1997, Magnificent Travel has specialized in professionally organized Turkey and Jordan Tours with transparent pricing, carefully selected hotels, licensed local guides, flexible itineraries, and reliable 24/7 local support. Our experienced destination specialists coordinate every detail, allowing you to travel confidently from arrival until your journey is complete.
